correctness.rationale: Direct orthogonal-conjugation computation gives the rank-one residual as a rational function of squared angular displacement; its derivative is strictly positive because a>b>0. Containment of a projective arc of length L in a centered arc establishes the exact deterministic minimax for every finite q, including L=pi. A uniform Gaussian input ray places the weak eigenvector in the parameter interval with probability L/pi; complement-gap geometry and inversion give the full CDF and its atom. Elementary tangent substitution proves the unpowered half-turn integral exactly pi*a*b. The packaged standard-library checker replayed successfully using rational matrices; finite angular grids and quadrature are supporting checks only. No unproved continuum limit is inferred from finite checks.

value.rationale: Addresses an explicit method-design gap: whether sharing one fixed random sketch column over a smooth, uniformly gapped matrix path ensures uniformly near-optimal rank-one approximation, and whether extra power iterations fix it. The sharp minimax, exact L/pi worst-error atom and full CDF quantify failure on short and long parameter intervals; the pathwise integrated loss ab and no-escape for any finite power depth identify substantive algorithmic and sample-budget consequences. Two sketch columns plus rank-one truncation removes the obstruction in this example. This is more than a routine pointwise residual calculation and does not claim arbitrary-dimensional generality.
